chunks: From him, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdillah ibn Jabalah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth of the Nāsib (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) and everything he owns is permissible for you, except his wife, for the marriage of the people of polytheism (Ahl al-Shirk) is valid. And this is because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Do not revile the people of polytheism, for every people have their own marriage customs." And if we did not fear for you that a man from you might be killed by a man from them, and the man from you is better than a thousand men from them and a hundred thousand of them, we would have commanded you to kill them for their sake, but that is up to the Imam.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الشِّرْكِ: Ahl al-Shirk: People of polytheism, used here as a comparison for the status of the Nāsib's wife.
key_terms.الإِمَامِ: Al-Imam: The divinely appointed leader, who holds the authority to command killing in this context.
key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: Nāsib: One who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt, often used for early opponents of Ali ibn Abi Talib.

ai.seo_question: Is the wealth and wife of a Nāsib halal for Muslims according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fiqh of *al-Nāsib* (those hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt), ruling that their wealth and property are generally permissible for Muslims to utilize, with the specific exception of their wives, whose marriage contracts are valid due to the principle that 'every people have their own marriage customs.' The Imam further contextualizes this by noting that while a single Muslim is spiritually superior to thousands of *Nāsib*, the command to kill them is reserved for the Imam to prevent communal retaliation, highlighting the political and juridical authority of the Imamate in managing enmity.
